title: Design a Large-Scale Recommendation System
prompt: Design a recommendation system that picks personalized items (feed posts, videos, or products) for hundreds of millions of users from a catalog of tens of millions of items. Cover candidate generation, ranking, the feature pipeline, embeddings, the online/offline split, and how you handle feedback loops and freshness.
blurb: The two-stage recsys — candidate generation and ranking, feature/embedding pipelines, online serving, and the feedback loop.

rubric.label: Requirements gathering
rubric.description: Separates functional (retrieve, rank, personalize, diversify) from non-functional (serving latency, freshness, throughput) and clarifies the business objective/metric being optimized.

rubric.label: Clarifying questions
rubric.description: Asks about the optimization objective (engagement, revenue, retention), user/item scale, latency budget, cold-start needs, and how success is measured (online metric).

rubric.label: Back-of-envelope estimations
rubric.description: Estimates request QPS, candidates per stage (millions → hundreds → tens), embedding index size, feature-store read fanout, and ranking model latency budget.

rubric.label: Candidate generation
rubric.description: Multiple retrieval sources — two-tower embeddings + ANN, collaborative filtering, popularity/recency, graph — narrowing millions of items to a few hundred cheaply.

rubric.label: Ranking
rubric.description: Heavy ranker scoring candidates with rich features, multi-task (click/like/dwell/convert) objectives, calibration, and re-ranking for diversity/business rules.

rubric.label: Feature pipeline
rubric.description: Batch + streaming features, a feature store with online/offline parity, point-in-time correctness for training, and freshness of real-time features.

rubric.label: Embeddings
rubric.description: Learning user/item embeddings (two-tower), keeping item embeddings fresh for new items, and serving them via an ANN index.

rubric.label: Online/offline split
rubric.description: Offline training + precompute vs online scoring; nearline updates; what's precomputed vs computed at request time.

rubric.label: Feedback loops & bias
rubric.description: Logging impressions/labels, position/exposure bias, popularity feedback loops, exploration, and delayed/implicit labels.

rubric.label: ML system specifics
rubric.description: Training/serving skew, model retraining cadence, cold-start strategy, offline-online metric alignment, and A/B evaluation.

rubric.label: Scaling
rubric.description: Sharding the ANN index and feature store, caching, precomputation, and horizontal scale of the ranking tier.

rubric.label: Observability & evaluation
rubric.description: Online metrics + guardrails, offline replay/NDCG, feature/prediction drift, and A/B testing infrastructure.

functional_requirements: Return a ranked, personalized list of items per user request
Retrieve candidates from multiple sources and rank them
Incorporate real-time user context (recent actions, session)
Handle new users and new items (cold start)
Apply business rules / diversity / dedup before returning
nonfunctional_requirements: Feature and item freshness (minutes for new items, seconds for session signals)
Consistent features between training and serving
Support frequent model retraining and A/B experiments
clarifying_questions: What are we optimizing — engagement, watch time, revenue, retention?
How many users and items, and what's the request QPS?
How important is cold-start (new items/users) and content freshness?
How do we measure success online, and can we A/B test?
Any hard business/policy constraints (diversity, dedup, blocked content)?
qualifying_questions: Is this a feed (many items) or single next-item recommendation?
Real-time personalization required, or is daily precompute acceptable?

estimations.traffic: 200M DAU x ~20 requests/day ≈ ~50k QPS avg, ~150k+ peak
estimations.funnel: Catalog ~50M → candidate generation ~500-1000 → ranking scores all → return top ~20
estimations.embedding_index: 50M item vectors x 128 dims x 4B ≈ 25GB — ANN index fits in RAM, sharded
estimations.feature_reads: Ranking ~500 candidates x dozens of features each = thousands of feature-store reads/request → must be batched/cached
estimations.ranker_budget: ~500 candidates scored within ~50ms → a compact DNN/GBDT with batched inference on GPU/CPU

core_components: Candidate generators (two-tower ANN, CF, popularity/recency, graph)
Model training + registry + A/B experiment framework
Logging pipeline (impressions, labels) for training and eval
data_model: interactions(user_id, item_id, action, dwell, position, ts) — event log
features_offline(entity_id, feature, value, event_ts) — point-in-time table
api_design: POST /recommend { user_id, context, count } → { items:[{item_id, score, reason}] }
POST /feedback { user_id, item_id, action, position, ts } → { ok }
Internal: POST /rank { user_id, candidate_ids } → scored list
reference.high_level_design: On a request, the service fetches the user's features/embedding from the online feature store and recent session signals from the streaming layer. Candidate generation runs several retrievers in parallel — a two-tower model embeds the user and does ANN lookup over item embeddings, plus collaborative-filtering, recently-popular, and graph sources — union/dedupe to a few hundred candidates. The ranking service pulls rich user x item x context features (batched from the feature store), scores all candidates with a multi-task model (predicting click/like/dwell/convert, calibrated and blended into one value), and a final re-ranker applies diversity, dedup, and business rules. Impressions and subsequent actions are logged to build training labels. Offline, models and item/user embeddings are retrained on point-in-time-correct features; embeddings and popularity candidates are precomputed nearline; the online path stays light. Everything ships behind A/B experiments measuring the north-star online metric.

deep_dives.probe: Explain the two-tower model and why candidate generation is a separate cheap stage. How do you retrieve a few hundred from 50M in single-digit ms, and how do you blend multiple retrieval sources?
How do you guarantee the features used at serving match training — online/offline parity — and get point-in-time correctness so you don't leak future information into labels?

Your logs are biased: users only click what you showed, and popular items get more exposure. How do you handle position/exposure bias and avoid a popularity feedback loop — exploration, inverse-propensity weighting?
You optimize multiple objectives (clicks, dwell, conversions). How do you combine them, calibrate probabilities, and avoid clickbait while hitting the business metric?
What's precomputed vs computed at request time? How fresh are item embeddings for an item uploaded 2 minutes ago (cold start)?
How often do you retrain, how do you detect that a deployed model has degraded (drift), and how do you validate a new model before full rollout?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions embeddings or two-tower or ANN or item vectors
followup_bank.question: When an item's attributes change or a new item is added, how do its embeddings stay in sync and become retrievable — nearline re-embedding, CDC from the catalog, index upsert? What's the freshness lag for a brand-new item?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions cache or caching or precompute
followup_bank.question: You cache per-user candidates or features. What's the eviction/TTL policy, and how do you avoid a stampede or serving stale recommendations right after the user's context changes?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions feature store or database or warehouse
followup_bank.question: How do features get from the source-of-truth data into the online store consistently — CDC/streaming vs batch materialization — and how do you avoid online/offline skew?
How do you detect model/feature drift in production and decide when to retrain or roll back?

scaling: Shard the ANN item index and replicate for QPS
Batch feature-store reads and cache hot user/item features
Precompute candidates/embeddings nearline; keep the request path light
Horizontally scale the stateless ranking tier; batch inference
Tiered candidate budgets to control cost at peak
bottlenecks: ANN retrieval latency and index freshness for new items
Ranking model latency on hundreds of candidates
Training/serving skew from divergent feature computation
tradeoffs: More candidates (recall/quality) vs ranking latency and cost
Fresher embeddings (nearline cost) vs staleness for new items
Single blended objective (simple) vs multi-task calibration (accurate)
alternative_solutions: Single-stage ranking (only viable for small catalogs)
Pure collaborative filtering / matrix factorization (weak on cold start, context)
Sequence/transformer models over session history for next-item prediction
observability: Online north-star metric + guardrails (diversity, complaints) via A/B
Offline replay metrics (NDCG, AUC, calibration) before rollout
Candidate-generation recall and ranking latency SLOs
Embedding freshness lag and cold-start coverage
security: Per-user data isolation and privacy (PII minimization in features)
Policy filtering of disallowed/unsafe items before serving
Auditability of why an item was recommended
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer first pins down the optimization objective and how it's measured online, then designs the classic two-stage funnel: cheap multi-source candidate generation (two-tower + ANN, CF, popularity, graph) narrowing 50M items to a few hundred, followed by a heavy multi-task ranker with rich, freshly-fetched features and a diversity/business re-ranker. It treats the feature pipeline as first-class — a feature store with online/offline parity and point-in-time correctness to avoid training/serving skew and label leakage — and explains the online/offline split (precompute embeddings/candidates nearline, keep the request path light). It confronts feedback loops directly (position/exposure bias, popularity loops, exploration/IPW), keeps item embeddings fresh for cold-start items, and validates every change via A/B tests with drift monitoring and offline replay. It names feature-read fanout, ranking latency, and feedback bias as the key bottlenecks.

interviewer_notes: Insist the candidate state the optimization objective and its online metric before designing — a recsys without a defined objective is a red flag. The two-stage funnel (candidate generation vs ranking) is table stakes; the senior signal is in the feature pipeline and feedback loops. Push the point-in-time-correctness / online-offline-parity probe hard — candidates who don't understand label leakage or training/serving skew are missing the core ML-systems hazard. The feedback-loop/bias deep dive separates strong candidates: expect position bias, popularity loops, and some exploration story. Use the embedding-freshness follow-up (new-item cold start, CDC from catalog) and the caching follow-up as interrupts. Reserve time for how they'd detect a degraded model in production (drift) and safely roll out via A/B.
